title.zh: 卷六十三 吳書十八 吳範劉惇趙達傳
title.en: Volume 63: Book of Wu 18 - Biographies of Wu Fan, Liu Dun, and Zhao Da
title.raw: 卷六十三 吳書十八 吳範劉惇趙達傳 Volume 63: Book of Wu 18 - Biographies of Wu Fan, Liu Dun, and Zhao Da

sentences.zh: 吳范字文則，會稽上虞人也。

translations.literal: Wu Fan, courtesy name Wenze, was a man of Shangyu in Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Fan, whose courtesy name was Wenze, came from Shangyu in Kuaiji Commandery.

sentences.zh: 以治歷數知風氣聞於郡中。

translations.literal: He became known in the commandery for mastering calendars and reckoning and reading winds and qi.
translations.idiomatic: He earned local renown for calendar science, numerology, and interpreting weather signs.

sentences.zh: 舉有道，詣京都，世亂不行。

translations.literal: Recommended as Abundant in the Way, he was summoned to the capital, but with the age in turmoil he did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended for the “Abundant in the Way” candidacy and called to the capital, he stayed home because the realm was in chaos.

sentences.zh: 會孫權起於東南，范委身服事，每有災祥，輒推數言狀。

translations.literal: When Sun Quan arose in the southeast Fan devoted himself to service; whenever omens of fortune or disaster appeared he always reckoned by numbers and stated their forms.
translations.idiomatic: After Sun Quan rose in the southeast Wu Fan entered his service—whenever heaven sent prodigies he cast figures and explained what they meant.

sentences.zh: 其術多效，遂以顯名。

translations.literal: His arts proved effective many times, and so he became famous.
translations.idiomatic: Again and again his calculations held, and his name spread.

sentences.zh: 初，權在吳，欲討黃祖。

translations.literal: At first, when Quan was at Wu and wished to campaign against Huang Zu,
translations.idiomatic: Early on, while Sun Quan held Wu and planned to attack Huang Zu,

sentences.zh: 范曰：“今茲少利，不如明年。

translations.literal: Fan said: “This year brings slight gain—it is not as good as next year.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Fan warned, “Victory this round would be small—wait until next year.”

sentences.zh: 明年戊子，荊州劉表亦身死國亡。

translations.literal: Next year is wuzi; in Jingzhou Liu Biao too will die and his state perish.
translations.idiomatic: The next year falls under wuzi—Liu Biao of Jingzhou will die and his domain collapse.”

sentences.zh: ”權遂征祖，卒不能克。

translations.literal: ” Quan then campaigned against Zu but could not overcome him.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan attacked anyway and failed to break Huang Zu.

sentences.zh: 明年，軍出，行及尋陽，范見風氣，因詣船賀，催兵急行，至即破祖，祖得夜亡。

translations.literal: The next year the army set out; reaching Xunyang Fan observed the qi, boarded a ship to congratulate Quan, and urged the troops to march hard—on arrival they broke Zu; Zu fled by night.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the fleet advanced; at Xunyang Wu Fan read the omens, boarded Sun Quan’s ship to offer congratulations, and pressed for speed—they smashed Huang Zu, who fled under cover of night.

sentences.zh: 權恐失之，范曰：“未遠，必生禽祖。

translations.literal: Quan feared losing him; Fan said: “He has not gone far—you will surely capture Zu alive.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan feared losing the prey; Wu Fan said, “Huang Zu cannot have gone far—you will take him alive.”

sentences.zh: ”至五更中，果得之。

translations.literal: ” By the fifth watch they indeed seized him.
translations.idiomatic: Before dawn broke they had him in hand.

sentences.zh: 劉表竟死，荊州分割。

translations.literal: Liu Biao died as predicted and Jingzhou was carved up.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Biao died on schedule and Jingzhou was partitioned.

sentences.zh: 及壬辰歲，范又白言：“歲在甲午，劉備當得益州。

translations.literal: In the renchen year Fan again reported: “When the year reaches jiawu, Liu Bei will obtain Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the renchen year Wu Fan added: “When the cycle reaches jiawu, Liu Bei will win Yizhou.”

sentences.zh: ”後呂岱從蜀還，遇之白帝，說備部眾離落，死亡且半，事必不克。

translations.literal: ” Later Lü Dai returned from Shu and met Quan at Baidi, reporting that Bei’s troops were scattered and half dead—the affair could not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Later Lü Dai came back from Shu and told Sun Quan at Baidi that Liu Bei’s army was shattered and half gone—the conquest would fail.

sentences.zh: 權以難范，范曰：“臣所言者天道也，而岱所見者人事耳。

translations.literal: Quan pressed Fan with this difficulty; Fan said: “What your servant speaks is Heaven’s way—what Dai saw is merely human affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan challenged him with Lü Dai’s report; Wu Fan replied, “I speak heaven’s pattern—Lü Dai saw only human circumstance.”

sentences.zh: ”備卒得蜀。

translations.literal: ” Bei ultimately obtained Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei took Shu just as predicted.

sentences.zh: 權與呂蒙謀襲關羽，議之近臣，多曰不可。

translations.literal: Quan plotted with Lü Meng to surprise Guan Yu; consulting close ministers, most said it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan and Lü Meng planned to ambush Guan Yu; most of his inner circle said no.

sentences.zh: 權以問范曰：“得之。

translations.literal: Quan asked Fan: “Will we obtain him?
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan asked Wu Fan, “Will we take him?”

sentences.zh: ”後羽在麥城，使使請降。

translations.literal: ” Later Yu was at Wheat Castle and sent envoys seeking surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Later Guan Yu holed up in Wheat Castle and offered submission.

sentences.zh: 權問范曰：“競當降否？

translations.literal: Quan asked Fan: “Will he truly surrender?
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan pressed, “Is the surrender genuine?”

sentences.zh: ”范曰：“彼有走氣，言降詐話耳。

translations.literal: ” Fan said: “He has the qi of flight—talk of surrender is deceit.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Fan answered, “His aura shows flight—the surrender talk is a lie.”

sentences.zh: ”權使潘璋邀其徑路，覘候者還，自羽已去。

translations.literal: ” Quan dispatched Pan Zhang to block his route; scouts returned reporting Yu had already gone.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan sent Pan Zhang to cut his retreat; scouts reported Guan Yu had slipped away.

sentences.zh: 范曰：“雖去不免。

translations.literal: Fan said: “Though he has gone he will not escape.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Fan insisted, “Even gone he cannot escape.”

sentences.zh: ”問其期，曰：“明日日中。

translations.literal: ” Asked the date, he said: “Tomorrow at noon.
translations.idiomatic: Asked when, he said, “Tomorrow at midday.”

sentences.zh: ”權立表下漏以待之。

translations.literal: ” Quan set a clepsydra beneath a gnomon and waited.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan set a water-clock under a sundial and waited.

sentences.zh: 及中不至，權問其故，范曰：“時尚未正中也。

translations.literal: When noon passed without event Quan asked the reason; Fan said: “The moment is not yet true noon.
translations.idiomatic: Midday came and went; Sun Quan demanded why—Wu Fan said, “True solar noon has not arrived.”

sentences.zh: ”頃之，有風動帷，范拊手曰：“羽至矣。

translations.literal: ” Presently wind stirred the curtains; Fan clapped his hands and said: “Yu has arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Soon a breeze rattled the drapes; Wu Fan cried, “Guan Yu is here.”

sentences.zh: ”須臾，外稱萬歲，傳言得羽。

translations.literal: ” Shortly voices outside shouted “Long live!”—word came that Yu had been taken.
translations.idiomatic: Moments later cheers rang outside—Guan Yu had been captured.

sentences.zh: 後權與魏為好，范曰：“以風氣言之，彼以貌來，其實有謀，宜為之備。

translations.literal: Later Quan made peace with Wei; Fan said: “Judging by qi they come with friendly faces but harbor plots—you should prepare.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Quan befriended Wei, Wu Fan warned, “Their winds bear smiles yet hide knives—brace yourself.”

sentences.zh: ”劉備盛兵西陵，范曰：“後當和親。

translations.literal: Liu Bei massed troops at Xiling; Fan said: “Later there will be marriage alliance.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Bei stacked armies at Xiling, Wu Fan said, “Peace through marriage will follow.”

sentences.zh: ”終皆如言。

translations.literal: ” All ended as he spoke.
translations.idiomatic: Every prediction landed.

sentences.zh: 其占驗明審如此。

translations.literal: His divinations were this clear and exact.
translations.idiomatic: His forecasts proved this precise.

sentences.zh: 權以范為騎都尉，領太史令，數從訪問，欲知其決。

translations.literal: Quan appointed Fan Colonel of Cavalry and concurrent Grand Clerk of Astrology, repeatedly consulting him and wishing to know his decisive methods.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan named him Colonel of Cavalry and Superintendent of Astrology, questioning him often and pressing for his inner formulas.

sentences.zh: 范秘惜其術，不以至要語權。

translations.literal: Fan closely guarded his arts and did not tell Quan the essentials.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Fan hoarded his secrets and never revealed the core techniques.

sentences.zh: 權由是恨之。

translations.literal: Thereupon Quan resented him.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan grew to resent him.

sentences.zh: 〈《吴录》曰：范独心计，所以见重者术，术亡则身弃矣，故终不言。〉

translations.literal: The Wu lu says: Fan relied on solitary calculation—what won esteem was the art; once the art vanished the body would be cast aside—hence he never spoke.
translations.idiomatic: The Record of Wu notes Wu Fan hoarded his craft because patrons valued only the magic—lose that and they discard you—so he stayed silent.

sentences.zh: 初，權為將軍時，范嘗白言“江南有王氣，亥子之間有大福慶。

translations.literal: At first, when Quan was General, Fan once reported: “South of the Yangzi bears kingly qi; between hai and zi great blessing will come.
translations.idiomatic: While Sun Quan still held the rank of general Wu Fan once said, “South of the river carries imperial vapors—between the hai and zi hours supreme fortune awaits.”

sentences.zh: ”權曰：“若終如言，以君為候。

translations.literal: ” Quan said: “If it ends as you say I shall enfeoff you as marquis.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan replied, “If it comes true I will make you a marquis.”

sentences.zh: ”及立為吳王，范時侍宴。

translations.literal: ” When he was invested King of Wu Fan attended a banquet.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Quan became King of Wu, Wu Fan waited on him at a feast.

sentences.zh: 曰：“昔在吳中，嘗言此事，大王識之邪？

translations.literal: He said: “Back in Wu I spoke of this—does Your Majesty remember?
translations.idiomatic: He asked, “Do you recall what I said back in Wu?”

sentences.zh: ”權曰：“有之。

translations.literal: ” Quan said: “It is so.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan answered, “I remember.”

sentences.zh: ”因呼左右，以侯綬帶范。

translations.literal: ” He called attendants to bring Fan a marquis’s ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered servants to present the marquis cords.

sentences.zh: 范權知權欲以厭當前言，輒手推不受。

translations.literal: Fan knew Quan wished to satisfy the earlier words with a gesture and pushed the gift away, refusing to accept.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Fan saw Sun Quan meant only to paper over an old promise and thrust the cords back untouched.

sentences.zh: 及後論功行封，以范為都亭侯，詔臨當出，權恚其愛道於己也，削除其名。

translations.literal: Later when merits were weighed for enfeoffment Fan was named Village Marquis; as the edict was about to issue Quan, furious that Fan loved his Dao more than himself, struck his name off.
translations.idiomatic: When rewards were handed out Wu Fan received a village marquisate; just before the edict Sun Quan, enraged that Wu Fan prized arcana above loyalty to him, erased his name.

sentences.zh: 范為人剛直，頗好自稱，然與親故交接有終始。

translations.literal: Fan was blunt by nature and inclined to boast, yet with kin and old friends his dealings had constancy from start to finish.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Fan was rigid and self-promoting, yet friendships with intimates lasted lifelong.

sentences.zh: 素與魏滕同邑相善。

translations.literal: From youth he was on good terms with Wei Teng of the same district.
translations.idiomatic: He had long been close to Wei Teng from his home county.

sentences.zh: 滕嘗有罪，權責怒甚嚴，敢有諫者死，范謂滕曰：“與汝偕死。

translations.literal: Teng once offended the law; Quan’s wrath was fierce—whoever remonstrated would die; Fan told Teng: “I die with you.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Teng once broke the law; Sun Quan’s rage terrified the court—death awaited any advisor—Wu Fan told him, “I perish at your side.”

sentences.zh: ”滕曰：“死而無益，何用死為？

translations.literal: ” Teng said: “Death without profit—what use is dying?
translations.idiomatic: Wei Teng answered, “Useless death helps nothing.”

sentences.zh: ”范曰：“安能慮此坐觀汝邪？

translations.literal: ” Fan said: “How could I sit watching you?
translations.idiomatic: Wu Fan shot back, “Could I sit idle while you hang?”

sentences.zh: ”乃髡頭自縛詣門下，使鈴下以聞。

translations.literal: ” Thereupon he shaved his head, bound himself, and presented himself at the gate, ordering the bell-man to announce him.
translations.idiomatic: He shaved his head, tied his own bonds, and appeared at the palace gate, telling the usher to announce him.

sentences.zh: 鈴下不敢，曰：“必死，不敢白。

translations.literal: The bell-man dared not, saying: “Certain death—I dare not report.
translations.idiomatic: The usher refused: “Reporting means death—I cannot.”

sentences.zh: ”范曰：“汝有子邪？

translations.literal: ” Fan said: “Do you have a son?
translations.idiomatic: Wu Fan asked, “Do you have children?”

translations.literal: ” He said: “Yes.
translations.idiomatic: “I do.”

sentences.zh: ”曰：“使汝為吳范死，子以屬我。

translations.literal: ” Fan said: “If you die for Wu Fan I entrust your son to me.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Fan said, “Die for me and I will raise your boy.”

sentences.zh: ”鈴下曰：“諾。

translations.literal: ” The bell-man said: “Agreed.
translations.idiomatic: The usher said, “Done.”

sentences.zh: ”乃排閣入。

translations.literal: ” He pushed through the gate.
translations.idiomatic: He burst through the gate.

sentences.zh: 言未卒，權大怒，欲便投以戟。

translations.literal: Before the words finished Quan was furious and wished at once to hurl a halberd at him.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan roared mid-sentence and reached for a halberd.

sentences.zh: 逡巡走出，范因突入，叩頭流血，言與涕並。

translations.literal: Hesitating he walked out; Fan then rushed in, knocking his head until it bled, speech and tears mingling.
translations.idiomatic: Attendants wavered and withdrew; Wu Fan darted in, beating his brow bloody, words lost in sobs.

sentences.zh: 良久，權釋，乃免滕。

translations.literal: After a long while Quan relented and spared Teng.
translations.idiomatic: After long moments Sun Quan relented and spared Wei Teng.

sentences.zh: 滕見范謝曰：“父母能生長我，不能免我於死。

translations.literal: Teng thanked Fan: “Parents bear and rear me yet cannot save me from death.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Teng told Wu Fan, “Parents give life but cannot spare me from execution.”

sentences.zh: 丈夫相知，如汝足矣，何用多為！

translations.literal: To know a man as you do contents a husband—what need of more!
translations.idiomatic: A friend like you satisfies a man—what more could I want?”

translations.literal: Closing quotation mark.
translations.idiomatic: This mark closes Wei Teng’s quoted speech.

sentences.zh: 〈《会稽典录》曰：滕字周林，祖父河内太守朗，字少英，列在八俊。

translations.literal: The Kuaiji dian lu says: Teng, courtesy name Zhoulin—his grandfather Lang was Administrator of Henei, courtesy name Shaoying, numbered among the Eight Heroes.
translations.idiomatic: The Kuaiji Canon records: Wei Teng, style Zhoulin—his grandfather Lang governed Henei as Shaoying, counted among the Eight Talents.

sentences.zh: 滕性刚直，行不苟合，虽遭困偪，终不回挠。

translations.literal: Teng’s nature was blunt; his conduct admitted no compromise; though pressed by hardship he never bent.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Teng was stubborn and principled; hardship never broke him.

sentences.zh: 初亦迕策，几殆，赖太妃救得免，语见《妃嫔传》。

translations.literal: At first he also crossed Ce and nearly perished—only the Senior Concubine’s rescue spared him; the tale appears in the Biographies of Imperial Concubines.
translations.idiomatic: He once defied Sun Ce and nearly died—Lady Wu saved him; see the concubine chapter.

sentences.zh: 历

translations.literal: The gloss reads li, introducing his successive offices.
translations.idiomatic: Continues the office list.

sentences.zh: （历山）

translations.literal: Parenthetical gloss reading Lishan.
translations.idiomatic: Editors note the alternate placename Lishan.

sentences.zh: 〔历阳〕、

translations.literal: Bracketed variant Liyang, followed by further enumeration.
translations.idiomatic: The variant reading Liyang heads the remaining appointments.

sentences.zh: （潘阳）

translations.literal: Parenthetical gloss reading Panyang.
translations.idiomatic: Scribes supply the alternate form Panyang for the county.

sentences.zh: 〔鄱阳〕、山阴三县令，鄱阳太守。〉

translations.literal: Bracketed Poyang; magistrate of three counties including Shanyin; Administrator of Poyang—end of gloss.
translations.idiomatic: The gloss concludes his offices in Poyang, three counties with Shanyin, then prefect of Poyang.

sentences.zh: 黃武五年，范病卒。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Huangwu Fan died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Huangwu 5 Wu Fan died of illness.

sentences.zh: 長子先死，少子尚幼，於是業絕。

translations.literal: His eldest son had predeceased him; the youngest was still a boy—thus his teaching ended.
translations.idiomatic: His firstborn had died; the youngest was a child—his lineage of arts died with him.

sentences.zh: 權追思之，募三州有能舉知術數如吳范、趙達者，封千戶侯，卒無所得。

translations.literal: Quan remembered him and offered across three provinces a thousand-household marquisate to whoever could match Wu Fan or Zhao Da in numerology—none was found.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan mourned him and promised a thousand-household marquisate to anyone who matched Wu Fan or Zhao Da’s skill—no one qualified.

sentences.zh: 〈《吴录》曰：范先知其死日，谓权曰：“陛下某日当丧军师。

translations.literal: The Wu lu says: Fan knew beforehand his death-day and told Quan: “Your Majesty will lose your army counselor on such-and-such a day.
translations.idiomatic: The Record of Wu adds: Wu Fan predicted his death and told Sun Quan, “You will lose your strategist on a set day.”

sentences.zh: ”权曰：“吾无军师，焉得丧之？

translations.literal: ” Quan said: “I have no army counselor—how can I lose him?
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan replied, “I employ no strategist—what loss is there?”

sentences.zh: ”范曰：“陛下出军临敌，须臣言而后行，臣乃陛下之军师也。

translations.literal: ” Fan said: “Whenever Your Majesty campaigns you await my word—your servant is Your Majesty’s strategist.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Fan answered, “When you march you wait on my counsel—I am your strategist.”

sentences.zh: ”至其日果卒。

translations.literal: ” On that day he indeed died.
translations.idiomatic: He died exactly then.

sentences.zh: 臣松之案，范死时，权未称帝，此云陛下，非也。〉

translations.literal: Pei Songzhi notes: When Fan died Quan had not yet taken the imperial title—the word “Your Majesty” here is incorrect.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi observes Sun Quan was not yet emperor when Wu Fan died—“Your Majesty” is anachronistic.

sentences.zh: 劉惇字子仁，平原人也。

translations.literal: Liu Dun, courtesy name Ziren, was a man of Pingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Dun, courtesy Ziren, hailed from Pingyuan.

sentences.zh: 遭亂避地，客游廬陵，事孫輔。

translations.literal: He fled turmoil and wandered to Luling as a guest, serving Sun Fu.
translations.idiomatic: He escaped chaos, lodged in Luling, and served Sun Fu.

sentences.zh: 以明天官達占數顯於南土。

translations.literal: He became eminent in the south through mastery of celestial offices and prognostic reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: Southern patrons esteemed him for astrology and divination math.

sentences.zh: 每有水旱寇賊，皆先時處期，無不中者。

translations.literal: Whenever flood, drought, or banditry struck he foretold the season beforehand—never missed.
translations.idiomatic: Floods, droughts, raids—he dated each before it arrived.

sentences.zh: 輔異焉，以為軍師，軍中鹹敬事之，號曰神明。

translations.literal: Fu marveled and appointed him army strategist; the entire army revered him and called him divine.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Fu named him strategist; the camp hailed him as a spirit.

sentences.zh: 建安中，孫權在豫章，時有星變，以問惇。

translations.literal: During the Jian’an era Sun Quan was at Yuzhang when stellar anomalies appeared—he questioned Dun.
translations.idiomatic: In Jian’an Sun Quan camped at Yuzhang; strange stars appeared and he consulted Liu Dun.

sentences.zh: 惇曰："災在丹楊。

translations.literal: Dun said: “Disaster lies in Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Dun said, “Calamity will strike Danyang.”

sentences.zh: "權曰："何如？

translations.literal: ” Quan said: “How so?
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan asked, “What form will it take?”

sentences.zh: "曰："客勝主人，到某日當得問。

translations.literal: ” He said: “The guest conquers the master—by such-and-such a day news will arrive.
translations.idiomatic: He answered, “The outsider bests the insider—you will hear by a set date.”

sentences.zh: "是時邊鴻作亂，卒如惇言。

translations.literal: ” At that time Bian Hong rebelled—it ended as Dun predicted.
translations.idiomatic: Then Bian Hong rose in revolt—exactly as Liu Dun foretold.

sentences.zh: 惇於諸術皆善，尤明太一，皆能推演其事，窮盡要妙，著書百餘篇，名儒刁玄稱以為奇。

translations.literal: Dun excelled in every art and especially understood the Taiyi method—he could unfold events from it to exhaust subtle essentials; he wrote more than a hundred chapters; the eminent scholar Diao Xuan praised them as marvelous.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Dun mastered many disciplines, especially Taiyi divination, unfolding cases to their subtle roots in over a hundred scrolls—scholar Diao Xuan called them extraordinary.

sentences.zh: 惇亦寶愛其術，不以告人，故世莫得而明也。

translations.literal: Dun also treasured his arts and told no one—hence the age could not understand them clearly.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Liu Dun hoarded his secrets, so posterity never fully grasped them.

sentences.zh: 趙達，河南人也。

translations.literal: Zhao Da was a man of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Da came from Henan.

sentences.zh: 少從漢侍中單甫受學，用思精密。

translations.literal: In youth he studied under Palace Attendant Shan Fu of Han, thinking with exquisite precision.
translations.idiomatic: Youth brought tutelage under Han Attendant Shan Fu; his reasoning ran fine-toothed.

sentences.zh: 謂東南有王者氣，可以避難，故脫身渡江。

translations.literal: He said the southeast bore an aura of kingship where one might flee disaster—therefore he crossed the Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: He read kingly qi in the southeast and crossed the river to escape turmoil.

sentences.zh: 治九宮一算之術，究其微旨，是以能應機立成。

translations.literal: He cultivated the nine-palace reckoning art, plumbing its subtle intent—thus he could answer on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: He perfected nine-palace calculation, grasped its marrow, and answered riddles instantly.

sentences.zh: 對問若神，至計飛蝗，射隱伏，無不中效。

translations.literal: His replies seemed supernatural—reckoning flying locusts or shooting hidden quantities—never failing.
translations.idiomatic: Whether counting flying locusts mid-flight or guessing concealed totals, he never missed.

sentences.zh: 或難達曰：飛者固不可校，誰知其然，此殆妄耳。

translations.literal: Someone challenged Da: flying things cannot be counted—who knows it true—this must be nonsense.
translations.idiomatic: Skeptics said airborne swarms cannot be tallied—his claims had to be fraud.

sentences.zh: "達使其人取小豆數鬥，播之席上，立處其數，驗覆果信。

translations.literal: ” Da had the man take several pecks of beans, scatter them on a mat, instantly stated the count, and verification by recount proved true.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Da poured beans across a mat, announced the total at once, and a recount proved him right.

sentences.zh: 嘗過知故，知故為之具食。

translations.literal: He once visited an old acquaintance who prepared food for him.
translations.idiomatic: Once he dropped on an old friend who laid out a meal.

sentences.zh: 食畢，謂曰："倉卒乏酒，又無佳看，無以敘意，如何?"達因取盤中只箸，再三從橫之，乃言："卿東壁下有美酒一斛，又有鹿肉三斤，何以辭無?"時坐有他賓，內得主人情。

translations.literal: When they finished eating he said: “Suddenly we lack wine and fine dishes—nothing to express good will—what can we do?” Da took the single chopsticks from the dish, crossed them again and again, then said: “East of your east wall lies a hu of fine wine and three jin of venison—why claim you have nothing?” Other guests were present and inwardly grasped the host’s embarrassment.
translations.idiomatic: After eating Zhao Da said they had no wine or delicacies—then took one chopstick, crossed it repeatedly, and declared a hu of wine and three jin of deer meat hid east of the east wall—though guests sat nearby and knew the host felt exposed.

sentences.zh: 主有慚曰："以卿善射有無，欲相試耳，竟效如此。

translations.literal: The host said ashamedly: “Because you excel at telling whether things exist or not I wished to try you—yet it came out thus.
translations.idiomatic: The host admitted embarrassment: “I meant only to test your gift for sensing what was hidden—it worked exactly as you claimed.”

sentences.zh: "遂出酒酣飲。

translations.literal: ” Thereupon he produced wine and they drank deep.
translations.idiomatic: They broke out the wine and drank freely.

sentences.zh: 又有書簡上作千萬數，著空倉中封之，令達算之。

translations.literal: Again someone wrote a sum to ten millions on paper, sealed it inside an empty granary, and ordered Da to reckon it.
translations.idiomatic: Another test wrote a huge figure on a slip, locked it in an empty granary, and told Zhao Da to divine the number.

sentences.zh: 達處如數，云："但有名無實。

translations.literal: Da stated the figure correctly and said: “There is only the reputation—no substance.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Da named the total and added, “The tally exists on paper—the granary stays empty.”

sentences.zh: "其精微若是。

translations.literal: ” His subtle craft reached such refinement.
translations.idiomatic: His precision ran that deep.

sentences.zh: 達寶惜其術，自闞澤、殷禮皆名儒善士，親屈節就學，達秘而不告，太史丞公孫滕少師事達，勤勞累年，達許教之者有年數矣，臨當喻語而輒復止。

translations.literal: Da treasured his arts—even Kan Ze and Yin Li, eminent scholars and upright men, humbled themselves to learn from him, yet Da kept silence and would not instruct them; Assistant Clerk of Astrology Gongsun Teng studied as his disciple from youth and labored many years—Da for several years promised to teach him, yet whenever about to explain he broke off again.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Da hoarded his methods: Kan Ze and Yin Li came as humble pupils yet learned nothing; Gongsun Teng toiled years as his disciple—each time Zhao Da neared disclosure he pulled back.

sentences.zh: 滕他日□酒具，侯顏色，拜跪而請。

translations.literal: Another day Teng prepared wine and fare, watched Da’s mood, knelt and pleaded.
translations.idiomatic: Another day Gongsun Teng laid out food and wine, read Zhao Da’s temper, and begged on his knees.

sentences.zh: 達曰："吾先人得此術，欲圖為帝王師，至仕來三世，不過太史郎，誠不欲復傳之。

translations.literal: Da said: “My forebears gained this art hoping to instruct emperors—yet three generations of office never rose past Clerk Astrologer—I truly shrink from handing it on.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Da answered, “Our ancestors meant this lore for dynastic tutors—three generations stalled at petty astrology posts—I hate passing it down.”

sentences.zh: 且此術微妙，頭乘尾除，一算之法，父子不相語。

translations.literal: Moreover the craft is subtle—multiply at the head, divide at the tail—one reckoning path—fathers and sons do not speak it between themselves.
translations.idiomatic: The method is delicate—operations compound and reduce—and families guard even one formula from kin.

sentences.zh: 然以子篤好不倦，今真以相授矣。

translations.literal: Yet because you love it earnestly without tiring, now I truly entrust it to you.
translations.idiomatic: Because you never slackened in zeal, I will actually teach you.”

sentences.zh: "飲酒數行，達起取素書兩眷，大如手指，達曰："當寫讀此，由自解也。

translations.literal: ” After several rounds of drinking Da rose and fetched two plain scrolls each the width of a finger; Da said: “Write them out and read—you will grasp them yourself.
translations.idiomatic: He rose after a few cups and produced two finger-sized booklets: “Copy these out—understanding will follow.”

sentences.zh: 吾久廢，不復省之。

translations.literal: I have neglected them long—I no longer review them.
translations.idiomatic: He claimed he had neglected the texts and barely remembered them.

sentences.zh: 今欲思論一過，數日當以相與。

translations.literal: Now I wish to think through them once—in a few days I shall give them to you.
translations.idiomatic: He asked for days to review before handing them over.”

sentences.zh: "滕如期往，至乃陽求索書，驚言失之，云："女婿昨來，必是渠所竊。

translations.literal: ” Teng arrived on time; Da pretended to hunt for the books and cried that they were lost, saying: “My son-in-law visited yesterday—he must have stolen them.
translations.idiomatic: When Gongsun Teng returned, Zhao Da feigned panic—the manuals were gone—blaming the son-in-law.

sentences.zh: "遂從此絕。

translations.literal: ” From this the instruction ceased.
translations.idiomatic: The lessons ended there.

sentences.zh: 初，孫權行師征伐，每令達有所推步，皆如其言。

translations.literal: At first when Sun Quan campaigned he always ordered Da to forecast events—they always matched his words.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Sun Quan marched he made Zhao Da cast ahead—and each forecast hit.

sentences.zh: 權問其法，達終不語，由此見薄，祿位不至。

translations.literal: Quan asked his method—Da never spoke—therefore he was slighted and salary and rank never rose.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan demanded the technique; Zhao Da stayed mute—so courtiers snubbed him and promotions stopped.

sentences.zh: 〈吴书曰：初，权即尊号，令达算作天子之后，当复几年？

translations.literal: The Wu shu says: When Quan first assumed the imperial title he ordered Da to reckon how many years remained under Heaven after the Son of Heaven—how many years until repetition?
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Wu adds that after Sun Quan took the throne he asked Zhao Da how long his mandate would run.

sentences.zh: 达曰：“高祖建元十二年，陛下倍之。

translations.literal: Da said: “Gaozu founded his reign-name in the twelfth year—Your Majesty doubles it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Da answered, “Han Gaozu began his era in the twelfth cycle—you will double that span.”

sentences.zh: ”权大喜，左右称万岁。

translations.literal: ” Quan rejoiced greatly; attendants shouted “Ten thousand years!”
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan cheered; the hall cried long life.

sentences.zh: 果如达言。〉

translations.literal: It indeed happened as Da said.
translations.idiomatic: Events matched Zhao Da’s reckoning.

sentences.zh: 達常笑謂諸星氣風術者曰："當回算帷幕，不出戶牖以知天道，而反晝夜暴露以望氣樣，不亦難乎!"閒居無為，引算自校，乃歎曰："吾算訖盡某年月日，其終矣。

translations.literal: Da often laughed at star-and-wind diviners: “You ought to reckon behind curtain and screen, know Heaven’s way without leaving doors and windows—yet you expose yourselves day and night watching qi—is it not painful!” Dwelling idle he pushed tallies and checked himself, then sighed: “My reckoning exhausts itself on such year month day—that is my end.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Da mocked outdoor astrologers—true skill needed no sky-gazing—then computed his own death date and sighed it aloud.

sentences.zh: "達妻數見達效，聞而哭泣。

translations.literal: Da’s wife had often witnessed Da’s efficacy—hearing this she wept.
translations.idiomatic: His wife had seen his arts work—she wept at the sentence.

sentences.zh: 達欲弭妻意，乃更步算，言："向者謬誤耳，尚未也。

translations.literal: Da wished to soothe his wife—he paced calculations again and said: “Earlier I erred—not yet.
translations.idiomatic: To calm her he recast the figures: “I miscalculated—the hour has not come.”

sentences.zh: "後如期死。

translations.literal: ” Later he died on that date.
translations.idiomatic: He died exactly when first predicted.

sentences.zh: 權聞達有書，求之不得，乃錄問其女，及發棺無所得，法術絕焉。

translations.literal: Hearing Da had writings Quan sought them without success—then interrogated his daughter—opening the coffin found nothing—the arts were extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan hunted Zhao Da’s manuscripts—questioned his daughter—opened the tomb—found nothing—the lineage of lore died.

sentences.zh: 〈吴录曰：皇象字休明，广陵江都人。

translations.literal: The Wu lu says: Huang Xiang, courtesy Xiuming, was a man of Jiangdu in Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: The Record of Wu names calligrapher Huang Xiang (style Xiuming) from Jiangdu.

sentences.zh: 幼工书。

translations.literal: Skilled in writing from youth.
translations.idiomatic: He practiced brushwork from boyhood.

sentences.zh: 时有张子并、陈梁甫能书。

translations.literal: At the time Zhang Zibing and Chen Liangfu could write.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zibing and Chen Liangfu were rivals in script.

sentences.zh: 甫恨逋，并恨峻，象斟酌其间，甚得其妙，中国善书者不能及也。

translations.literal: Liangfu resented Bu, Zibing resented Jun—Xiang mediated between them and grasped the exquisite point—calligraphers of the Central Plains could not equal him.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Xiang balanced their styles and surpassed both—northern masters fell short.

sentences.zh: 严武字子卿，卫尉畯再从子也，围釭莫与为辈。

translations.literal: Yan Wu, courtesy Ziqing—grand-nephew twice removed of Commandant of the Guards Jun—none matched him in seal-ring engraving.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Wu (Ziqing), great-grandson of Wei officer Yan Jun, stood alone in bronze-seal carving.

sentences.zh: 宋寿占梦，十不失一。

translations.literal: Song Shou interpreted dreams—missed one in ten.
translations.idiomatic: Song Shuo dream-divined with ninety-percent accuracy.

sentences.zh: 曹不兴善画，权使画屏风，误落笔点素，因就以作蝇。

translations.literal: Cao Buxing excelled at painting—Quan had him paint a screen—by mistake ink dropped on silk—thereupon he turned it into a fly.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered to paint a screen Cao Buxing smeared ink—turned the blot into a fly.

sentences.zh: 既进御，权以为生蝇，举手弹之。

translations.literal: When presented Quan thought it a living fly and raised his hand to flick it.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan tried to swat the painted fly.

sentences.zh: 孤城郑妪能相人，及范、惇、达八人，世皆称妙，谓之八绝云。

translations.literal: Old woman Zheng of Gucheng could read faces—with Fan, Dun, Da and five others the age called them the Eight Marvels.
translations.idiomatic: Physiognomist Mother Zheng of lone-walled Gucheng joined Wu Fan, Liu Dun, Zhao Da, and five talents hailed as the Eight Wonders.

sentences.zh: 《晋阳秋曰：吴有葛衡字思真，明达天官，能为几巧，作浑天，使地居于中，以机动之，天转而地止，以上应晷度。〉

translations.literal: The Jin Yang Qiu says: Wu had Ge Heng, courtesy Sizhen—understood celestial offices—crafted ingenious devices—made an armillary sphere with earth at the center moved by gears—heaven turned while earth stood still—matching sundial degrees.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin Yang Qiu credits Ge Heng with a geared cosmos-model matching celestial arcs.

translations.literal: 【Appraisal】
translations.idiomatic: Section heading: Appraisal.

sentences.zh: 評曰：三子各於其術精矣，其用思妙矣，然君子等役心神，宜於大者遠者，是以有識之士，捨彼而取此也。

translations.literal: The appraisal says: Each of the three men mastered his craft—their application of mind was subtle—yet the gentleman employs spirit on great and distant aims—therefore discerning scholars forsake the former and embrace the latter.
translations.idiomatic: The historian concludes: technical genius tempts petty wonders; thoughtful men aim higher.

sentences.zh: 〈孙盛曰：夫玄览未然，逆鉴来事，虽裨灶、梓慎其犹病诸，况术之下此者乎？

translations.literal: Sun Sheng said: To survey the unseen and mirror coming events—even Pi Zao and Zi Shen struggled—how much more arts beneath theirs?
translations.idiomatic: Sun Sheng notes even canonical astrologers stumbled—lesser tricks merit doubt.

sentences.zh: 吴史书达知东南当有王气，故轻举济江。

translations.literal: The Wu history says Da knew kingly qi would rise in the southeast—therefore he lightly crossed the Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: Wu records say Zhao Da crossed south chasing imperial vapors.

sentences.zh: 魏承汉绪，受命中畿，达不能豫睹兆萌，而流窜吴越。

translations.literal: Wei inherited Han’s thread and received mandate in the heartland—Da failed to foresee the budding sign beforehand and drifted among Wu and Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Wei held the Central Plain—yet Zhao Da missed Wei’s rise and wandered eastern marshes.

sentences.zh: 又不知吝术之鄙，见薄於时，安在其能逆睹天道而审帝王之符瑞哉？

translations.literal: Again ignorant how base it is to hoard arts—slighted by the age—where lies ability to foresee Heaven’s way and discern imperial portents?
translations.idiomatic: Sun Sheng asks how a stingy technician could read dynastic fate.

sentences.zh: 昔圣王观天地之文，以画八卦之象，故亹亹成於蓍策，变化形乎六爻，是以三易虽殊，卦繇理一，安有回转一筹，可以钩深测隐，意对逆占，而能遂知来物者乎？

translations.literal: Ancient sage kings observed Heaven and Earth’s patterns to fashion the eight trigrams—thus abundant wisdom arose from milfoil and transformation took form in six lines—therefore though three Changes differ hexagram principle is one—how could rotating one tally hook depths and probe concealments or invert divination face-to-face and thereby know future things?
translations.idiomatic: The classics unified oracle logic—no single abacus replaces the Changes.

sentences.zh: 流俗好异，妄设神奇，不幸之中，仲尼所弃，是以君子志其大者，无所取诸。

translations.literal: Common fashion loves the strange and vainly fabricates marvels—among ill omens Confucius discarded these—therefore the gentleman sets his aim on greatness and takes nothing from such.
translations.idiomatic: Fashion craves miracles—Confucius spurned fortune-telling—the gentleman thinks bigger.

sentences.zh: 臣松之以为盛云“君子志其大者，无所取诸”，故评家之旨，非新声也。

translations.literal: Pei Songzhi considers: When Sheng says “the gentleman aims at greatness and takes nothing from such”—the appraiser’s meaning is no novelty.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi notes Sun Sheng echoes the official appraisal.

sentences.zh: 其餘所讥，则皆为非理。

translations.literal: His remaining ridicule is altogether unreasonable.
translations.idiomatic: Pei rejects Sun Sheng’s other barbs.

sentences.zh: 自中原酷乱，至于建安，数十年间，生民殆尽，比至小康，皆百死之餘耳。

translations.literal: From central plains cruel chaos until Jian’an—within several decades the living nearly vanished—by modest peace all were survivors of hundred deaths.
translations.idiomatic: Decades of northern slaughter left few survivors—peace meant beating overwhelming odds.

sentences.zh: 江左虽有兵革，不能如中国之甚也，焉知达不算其安危，知祸有多少，利在东南，以全其身乎？

translations.literal: Though east of the river knew warfare it could not match China’s severity—how know Da did not reckon safety and danger, weigh harm’s measure, and judge profit lay in the southeast to preserve himself?
translations.idiomatic: The south suffered less—Zhao Da may simply have sought safer ground.

sentences.zh: 而责不知魏氏将兴，流播吴越，在京房之筹，犹不能自免刑戮，况达但以秘术见薄，在悔吝之间乎！

translations.literal: Yet blame him for not foreknowing Wei’s rise and drifting Wu-Yue—even Jing Fang’s reckonings could not spare execution—how much more Da slighted only for secret arts—between regret and miserliness!
translations.idiomatic: Pinning prophets for politics ignores worse failures—even masters died under suspicion.

sentences.zh: 古之道术，盖非一方，探赜之功，岂惟六爻，苟得其要，则可以易而知之矣，回转一筹，胡足怪哉？

translations.literal: Ancient arts were not one path—work plumbing mysteries used not only six lines—grasp the essentials and you know through Change—rotating one tally—what is strange?
translations.idiomatic: Many roads led to insight—the Changes were broader than one chip.

sentences.zh: 达之推算，穷其要妙以知幽测隐，何愧于古！

translations.literal: Da’s reckonings exhausted subtle essentials to probe depths—what shame before antiquity?
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Da plumbed secrets as well as ancients.

sentences.zh: 而以裨、梓限之，谓达为妄，非笃论也。

translations.literal: Yet limiting him with Pi and Zi—calling Da deluded—is not serious judgment.
translations.idiomatic: Equating him with Pi Zao sells Zhao Da short.

sentences.zh: 《抱朴子》曰：时有葛仙公者，每饮酒醉，常入人家门前陂水中卧，竟日乃出。

translations.literal: The Baopuzi says: Immortal Lord Ge when drunk would lie in pond water before people’s gates all day before emerging.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Hong tells how Immortal Ge dozed in roadside ponds.

sentences.zh: 曾从吴主别，到洌州，还遇大风，百官船多没，仙公船亦沉沦，吴主甚怅恨。

translations.literal: Once bidding farewell to the Wu lord—reaching Liezhou—a great wind sank many boats—including his—the Wu lord deeply regretted.
translations.idiomatic: Returning from court Ge Hong’s boat sank in a gale—Sun Quan mourned.

sentences.zh: 明日使人钩求公船，而登高以望焉。

translations.literal: Next day men grappled for the boat while watchers climbed high to scan.
translations.idiomatic: Next day crews dragged for wreckage from the heights.

sentences.zh: 久之，见公步从水上来，衣履不沾，而有酒色。

translations.literal: After long delay they saw him walking from the water—clothes dry—with wine-flushed face.
translations.idiomatic: He walked ashore dry and tipsy.

sentences.zh: 既见而言曰：“臣昨侍从而伍子胥见请，暂过设酒，忽忽不得，即委之。

translations.literal: Seeing him he said: “Yesterday my attendant Wu Zixu invited me—I stopped for wine—could not linger—had to leave.
translations.idiomatic: He blamed a banquet with Wu Zixu’s ghost for his delay.”

sentences.zh: ”又有姚光者，有火术。

translations.literal: ” Also Yao Guang practiced fire arts.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Guang commanded flame.

sentences.zh: 吴主身临试之，积荻数千束，使光坐其上，又以数千束荻裹之，因猛风而燔之。

translations.literal: The Wu lord personally tested—stacked thousands of reed bundles—had Guang sit atop—wrapped thousands more—blazed them with fierce wind.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan piled reeds, seated Yao Guang, torched the heap.

sentences.zh: 荻了尽，谓光当以化为烬，而光端坐灰中，振衣而起，把一卷书。

translations.literal: When reeds burned out they expected Guang reduced to ash—yet Guang sat upright in ashes—shook his robes and rose—holding a scroll.
translations.idiomatic: Ash fell away—Yao Guang stood untouched with a book.

sentences.zh: 吴主取其书视之，不能解也。

translations.literal: The Wu lord took the book—could not decipher it.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan could not read the script.

sentences.zh: 又曰：吴景帝有疾，求觋视者，得一人。

translations.literal: Also: Wu Jingdi fell ill—sought a spirit medium—found one.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jing of Wu sought healers—found a medium.

sentences.zh: 景帝欲试之，乃杀鹅而埋於苑中，架小屋，施床几，以妇人屐履服物著其上，乃使觋视之。

translations.literal: Jingdi wished to test—killed a goose buried in the garden—built a hut—bed and desk—placed woman’s shoes and garments atop—sent the medium to view.
translations.idiomatic: He staged a fake tomb with goose remains and women’s gear.

sentences.zh: 告曰：“若能说此冢中鬼妇人形状者，当加赏而即信矣。

translations.literal: Told him: “If you can describe this tomb ghost woman’s shape—you shall be rewarded and trusted.
translations.idiomatic: Success meant reward—describe the ghost woman.

sentences.zh: ”竟日尽夕无言，帝推问之急，乃曰：“实不见有鬼，但见一头白鹅立墓上，所以不即白之，疑是鬼神变化作此相，当候其真形而定。

translations.literal: ” All day to evening no word—the emperor pressed urgently—then said: “Truly saw no ghost—only a white goose on the tomb—did not report immediately—suspected spirit disguise—waited for true form.
translations.idiomatic: The medium stalled—then admitted seeing only a goose—feared spirits mimicking women.

sentences.zh: 无复移易，不知何故，不敢不以实上闻。

translations.literal: No further change—know not why—dare report only truth.
translations.idiomatic: He feared deceiving the throne.

sentences.zh: ”景帝乃厚赐之。

translations.literal: ” Jingdi richly rewarded.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor paid him well.

sentences.zh: 然则鹅死亦有鬼也。

translations.literal: Thus even a dead goose has a ghost?
translations.idiomatic: Pei wonders whether geese have ghosts.

sentences.zh: 葛洪《神仙传》曰：仙人介象，字元则，会稽人，有诸方术。

translations.literal: Ge Hong’s Traditions of Immortals says: Immortal Jie Xiang, courtesy Yuanze—Kuaiji—commanded many arts.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Hong’s hagiography introduces Jie Xiang of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 吴主闻之，徵象到武昌，甚敬贵之，称为介君，为起宅，以御帐给之，赐遗前后累千金，从象学蔽形之术。

translations.literal: The Wu lord summoned him to Wuchang—honored him—styled Lord Jie—built a mansion—granted imperial curtains—gifts piled to thousand gold—studied invisibility from Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan housed him in luxury and studied concealment.

sentences.zh: 试还后宫，及出殿门，莫有见者。

translations.literal: Tested returning through rear palace—exiting hall gate—none saw him.
translations.idiomatic: He vanished crossing palace gates.

sentences.zh: 又使象作变化，种瓜菜百果，皆立生可食。

translations.literal: Also had Xiang perform transformations—plant melons vegetables hundred fruits—all sprouted instantly edible.
translations.idiomatic: He sprouted melons and fruits on command.

sentences.zh: 吴主共论鲙鱼何者最美，象曰：“鯔鱼为上。

translations.literal: The Wu lord debated which sliced fish excelled—Xiang said: “Zi fish ranks highest.
translations.idiomatic: Asked about sashimi, Jie Xiang praised zi fish.

sentences.zh: ”吴主曰：“论近道鱼耳，此出海中，安可得邪？

translations.literal: The Wu lord said: “Speaking of nearby river fish—this comes from the sea—how obtain?
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan called sea fish unattainable inland.

sentences.zh: ”象曰：“可得耳。

translations.literal: ” Xiang said: “Can obtain.
translations.idiomatic: Jie Xiang promised delivery.

sentences.zh: ”乃令人於殿庭中作方埳，汲水满之，并求钩。

translations.literal: ” Thereupon ordered a square pit dug in the courtyard—filled with water—and sought hooks.
translations.idiomatic: Servants dug a pool and fetched tackle.

sentences.zh: 象起饵之，垂纶於埳中。

translations.literal: Xiang baited—cast line into the pit.
translations.idiomatic: He angled in the courtyard pool.

sentences.zh: 须臾，果得鯔鱼。

translations.literal: Presently obtained zi fish.
translations.idiomatic: He landed a zi fish.

sentences.zh: 吴主惊喜，问象曰：“可食不？

translations.literal: The Wu lord delighted—asked: “Edible?
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan asked if it was safe to eat.

sentences.zh: ”象曰：“故为陛下取以作生鲙，安敢取不可食之物！

translations.literal: ” Xiang said: “Fetched for Your Majesty as raw slices—how dare bring inedible!
translations.idiomatic: Jie Xiang swore it suited sashimi.

sentences.zh: ”乃使厨下切之。

translations.literal: ” Ordered the kitchen to slice.
translations.idiomatic: Chefs carved the fish.

sentences.zh: 吴主曰：“闻蜀使来，得蜀姜作赍甚好，恨尔时无此。

translations.literal: The Wu lord said: “Heard Shu envoys brought Shu ginger—excellent—regret none then.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan craved Shu ginger with the meal.

sentences.zh: ”象曰：“蜀姜岂不易得，原差所使者，并付直。

translations.literal: ” Xiang said: “Shu ginger not hard to obtain—wish to assign messenger—pay the price.
translations.idiomatic: Jie Xiang promised instant ginger.

sentences.zh: ”吴主指左右一人，以钱五十付之。

translations.literal: ” The Wu lord pointed to an attendant—gave fifty cash.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan picked a runner and fifty coins.

sentences.zh: 象书一符，以著青竹杖中，使行人闭目骑杖，杖止，便买姜讫，复闭目。

translations.literal: Xiang wrote a charm—placed it in a green bamboo staff—had the traveler close eyes and ride the staff—when the staff stopped buy ginger—close eyes again.
translations.idiomatic: He charmed a bamboo rod for blind teleport shopping.

sentences.zh: 此人承其言骑杖，须臾止，已至成都，不知是何处，问人，人言是蜀市中，乃买姜。

translations.literal: The man obeyed—presently stopped—already at Chengdu—did not know where—asked—people said Shu market—bought ginger.
translations.idiomatic: The courier opened his eyes in Chengdu’s market.

sentences.zh: 于时吴使张温先在蜀，既於市中相识，甚惊，便作书寄其家。

translations.literal: At that time Wu envoy Zhang Wen was in Shu—recognized him in the market—startled—wrote a letter home.
translations.idiomatic: He met Zhang Wen and sent mail east.

sentences.zh: 此人买姜毕，捉书负姜，骑杖闭目，须臾已还到吴，厨下切鲙適了。

translations.literal: The man finished buying ginger—took letter carried ginger—rode staff eyes closed—instantly back in Wu—the kitchen finished slicing fish.
translations.idiomatic: He returned before the cooks finished—ginger in hand.

sentences.zh: 臣松之以为葛洪所记，近为惑众，其书文颇行世，故撮取数事，载之篇末也。

translations.literal: Pei Songzhi considers Ge Hong’s records approach deluding masses—the text circulates widely—therefore excerpt several matters at chapter end.
translations.idiomatic: Pei cites Ge Hong to show wonder-tales entertained readers—not sober history.

sentences.zh: 神仙之术，讵可测量，臣之臆断，以为惑众，所谓夏虫不知冷冰耳。〉

translations.literal: Immortal arts—how measure—my opinion judges them deluding masses—the so-called summer insects knowing nothing of ice—end quote.
translations.idiomatic: Pei dismisses miracle lore as summer worms denying winter—closing the gloss.”
